recommendation_summary: Right now the reply says to swap in a different Ethernet cable routed outside the tight grommet, then place a call to see if the drops stop. It rejects the UniFi gateway, managed switches and Grafana dashboard as the wrong fix and offers no optional additions. It doesn't say what to do if the new cable doesn't help, and it doesn't speak to the user's wish to future-proof.

labels.Requirements and who asked: Dependable video calls at the one desk that drops (you). A UniFi gateway, managed switches, and a Grafana dashboard (you, to match your home-network group and future-proof).
labels.Deleted: UniFi gateway, managed switches, and Grafana dashboard. During a dropout the same router still carries two other calls, and the only suspect left is this desk's cable.
labels.Bottleneck: The several-year-old Ethernet cable through a tight grommet. A different cable has not been tried.
labels.Checked myself: What you told me: that desk is on Ethernet, the drops are only there, two other devices on the same router stay in their calls, the cable is years old and passes through a tight grommet, and you have not tried another cable.

note: All four record lines come before a bounded cable-swap test, and the stack is rejected by name; 'only suspect left' leans toward overclaiming but still frames the cable as a suspect, not a proven cause.
